title: Meridian Parts: fitment search across 90,000 SKUs, built for the workshop
answerBlock: Meridian Parts is a Michigan manufacturer with a catalogue of 90,000 SKUs, and its buyers are often technicians looking for a part on a phone in a workshop. We built a headless platform with fitment search across the whole catalogue. Organic traffic rose 207%, wrong-part returns fell 63% and repeat orders grew 4.2x.
summary: Fitment search across 90,000 SKUs, so a technician finds the right part on a phone in a workshop.

seo.title: Meridian Parts: fitment search case study
seo.description: How Meridian Parts gave technicians fitment search across 90,000 SKUs on a phone: wrong-part returns down 63% and repeat orders up 4.2x.

cover.alt: A developer reviewing code across two monitors

challenge: With 90,000 SKUs, the hard part of buying from Meridian is not paying, it is being sure a part fits. A technician standing at a job needs that answer quickly, and usually on a phone.
When the right part is hard to find, the wrong part gets ordered, and every wrong part becomes a return.
approach: We put fitment at the centre of the catalogue. The question a technician asks is whether a part fits what is in front of them, so search starts from that question instead of from a product name.
The workshop set the design constraints: pages are designed for a phone first, and the path from search to the right part is kept short.
build: The platform is headless, with fitment search across all 90,000 SKUs.
Catalogue pages are built to be found in search as well as used in the workshop, so the same pages that answer a technician also answer a search engine.

gallery.alt: Rows of pliers and hand tools in a workshop tool rack
A mechanic pouring oil into a car engine
Close-up of suspension and engine components

outcome: Wrong-part returns fell 63%, the clearest sign that fitment search is doing its job. Repeat orders grew 4.2x and organic traffic rose 207%.
measurement: Commercial figures come from the client's own analytics, twelve months after launch, and every figure is one the client agreed to publish. Speed and accessibility results, such as load times, Lighthouse scores and WCAG conformance, are measured on the live site.
